title: Associate Director, Program Supply Chain
description:
About AbbVie
AbbVie's mission is to discover and deliver innovative medicines and solutions that solve serious health issues today and address the medical challenges of tomorrow. We strive to have a remarkable impact on people's lives across several key therapeutic areas including immunology, oncology and neuroscience - and products and services in our Allergan Aesthetics portfolio. For more information about AbbVie, please visit us at  www.abbvie.com . Follow @abbvie on  LinkedIn,   Facebook ,  Instagram ,  X  and  YouTube.
The Associate Director, Program Supply Chain is responsible for leading the end-to-end establishment and management of external clinical drug product manufacturing partnerships supporting pharmaceutical development programs. The position serves as the primary operational relationship lead for designated third-party manufacturers and provides project and supplier management leadership from initial supplier engagement and onboarding through manufacturing execution, product release, and delivery to AbbVie.
The role leads cross-functional teams to establish new third-party manufacturing relationships, define project requirements, coordinate agreements and supplier readiness, develop integrated project plans, and oversee execution against program objectives. The position ensures that external manufacturing activities are effectively planned and executed to meet quality, regulatory, schedule, supply, and financial expectations.
The Associate Director leads a team of approximately 5–7 direct reports responsible for project and supplier management activities. The position is accountable for establishing clear priorities, developing organizational capability, coaching and developing talent, and ensuring effective deployment of resources across the external manufacturing portfolio.
Through direct people leadership and cross-functional matrix leadership, the Associate Director proactively identifies and mitigates project and supply risks, manages supplier performance, drives issue resolution and continuous improvement, and ensures effective communication and escalation to senior leadership.
Responsibilities:
Lead establishment and onboarding of new third-party manufacturing partners
Serve as the primary operational relationship lead for assigned third-party manufacturers
Lead cross-functional project teams supporting external manufacturing
Provide end-to-end project oversight of third-party drug product manufacturing
Represent projects at supplier governance and manage supplier performance
Lead proactive project and supply risk management
Coordinate contractual activities supporting external manufacturing D
Drive cross-functional issue resolution and provide program visibility to leadership
Lead, develop, and build capabilities within a team of 5–7 project and supplier management professionals
Drive continuous improvement of the external manufacturing operating model
Bachelor’s Degree in Science or Engineering or related degree, required; MBA or higher education desired but not required
10+ years Pharmaceutical, Device Engineering or Operations Experience preferred
6+ years of Program Management Experience
Project Risk Management
Demonstrated success as a collaborative team player
Proven ability to communicate and deliver results, actions, decisions and concerns with little direction or supervision in a timely manner
Broad, diverse, cross-functional or cross-divisional experience
Ability to think strategically and creatively

description:

Purpose
Manages other Medical and/or Scientific Directors and leads the direction, planning, execution, and interpretation of clinical trials or research activities of one or more clinical development programs. Participates in and may lead cross-functional teams to generate, deliver, and disseminate high-quality clinical data supporting overall product scientific and business strategy.
Responsibilities
Personally or through a direct report, leads and demonstrates ownership of the design and implementation of multiple clinical development programs (or one large, complex program) in support of the overall product development plan, based on strong medical and scientific principles, knowledge of compliance and regulatory requirements, AbbVie’s customers, markets, business operations, and emerging issues. Oversees project-related education of investigators, study site personnel.
Has overall responsibility for leading and mentoring clinical study teams, monitoring overall study integrity, and review, interpretation, and communication of accumulating data pertaining to safety and efficacy of the molecule. Along with Clinical Operations, is responsible for ensuring agreed-upon study enrollment and overall timelines for key deliverables. Responsible for assessment and reporting of serious adverse events per corporate policy and regulations for those protocols assigned.
Has primary responsibility for and ownership of design, analysis, interpretation, and reporting of scientific content of protocols, Investigator Brochures, Clinical Study reports, regulatory submissions and responses, and other program documents.
Manages one level of Medical and Scientific Directors (typically 2 to 4) and/or Clinical Scientists. This responsibility involves direct oversight of clinical development activities and/or management of personnel who may be working on other projects. Responsible for hiring, onboarding, mentoring, training, and supporting career development of these individuals.
May chair Clinical Strategy Team(s), with responsibility for development of a rigorous, cross-functionally-aligned, vetted Clinical Development Plan with full consideration of contingencies and alternative approaches. In this capacity, responsibilities may include supervision of matrix team members and serving as the Clinical Research representative to lend clinical development and medical expertise to Asset Development Teams (ADTs) and ADT Leadership Boards (ALBs).
Serves as the in-house clinical expert for one or more molecules and diseases in the therapeutic area, coordinating and leading appropriate scientific activities with internal stakeholders as they relate to ongoing projects. May participate in or lead clinical development contributions to due diligence or other business development activity. As required by program needs, contributes in partnership with Discovery colleagues to design and implementation of translational strategies.
Acts as clinical lead and actively solicits opinion leader interactions related to the disease area(s); partners with Medical Affairs, Commercial and other functions in these activities as required, consistent with corporate policies, to ensure that broad cross-functional perspectives are incorporated into Clinical Development Plans and protocols as appropriate.
Stays abreast of professional information and technology through conferences, medical literature, and other available training, to augment expertise in the therapeutic area. May represent AbbVie at key external meetings.
Responsible for understanding the regulatory requirements related to the clinical studies and global drug development and accountable for complying with those requirements. Serves as a clinical representative for key regulatory discussions.
Ensures adherence to Good Clinical Practices, pharmacovigilance standards, standard operating procedures and to all other quality standards in conducting research.
Medical Doctor (M.D.), Doctor of Osteopathy (D.O.), or non-US equivalent of M.D. degree with relevant therapeutic specialty in an academic or hospital environment required. Completion of a residency program strongly preferred. Completion of a subspecialty fellowship is desirable.
At least 7 years (9+ years preferred) of clinical trial experience in the pharmaceutical industry, academia, or equivalent.
Respiratory experience strongly preferred.
Ability to run a complex clinical research program independently.
Proven leadership skills and ability to bring out the best in others on a cross-functional global team. Must be able to lead and manage through influence.
Demonstrated commitment to training and development of junior-level staff, using best judgment to assure that they work with an appropriate level of autonomy.
Ability to interact externally and internally to support a global scientific and business strategy.
Extensive knowledge of clinical trial methodology, regulatory and compliance requirements governing clinical trials, and experience in development of clinical strategy and the design of study protocols.

Ability to exercise judgment and address complex problems and create solutions across multiple projects.

title: Battery Modeling Engineer
description:
ABOUT BASE

Base is America’s next-generation power company. We’re rebuilding the foundation of modern civilization–electricity–by deploying a vast network of distributed batteries that is transforming today’s fragile, centralized grid into a resilient and abundant system. We are engineers, operators, and creatives solving some of the most complex, interdisciplinary challenges of our time.




ABOUT THE ROLE

As a Battery Modeling Engineer, you’ll build the data and degradation models that tell us how our batteries age in the real world. You’ll combine software engineering, data science, and semi-empirical degradation modeling, turning telemetry from our fleet of deployed home batteries and data from cell-level testing into trusted datasets and models that predict capacity fade, resistance growth, and remaining useful life across the conditions our batteries actually see.

This is a hybrid role at the intersection of software, data science, and battery science. You’ll own degradation analytics end to end, from the pipelines and data models that make fleet and lab data trustworthy to the semi-empirical models and tools the rest of Base relies on, and you’ll help found and set up Base’s cell characterization lab. Your work will directly shape how we operate our fleet and plan for its long-term performance.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Build and validate semi-empirical degradation models (calendar and cycle aging, capacity fade, resistance growth) for the cells in our fleet.

 - Help found and set up Base’s cell characterization lab: define test plans, select equipment, and stand up the processes that generate reliable aging data.

 - Analyze fleet- and device-level data to understand how temperature, state of charge, and usage patterns drive degradation, and validate model predictions against real-world behavior.

 - Turn model outputs into tools and insights that engineering, fleet, and markets teams use to decide how our batteries are operated.

 - Write production-quality Python and SQL (or equivalent), with the tests, documentation, and monitoring that keep models trustworthy as the fleet grows and ages.

 - Track model history and communicate those changes effectively across the organization.




WHAT YOU'LL BRING

 - A background in Chemistry or Battery Physics or a related field such as electrochemistry, materials science, or chemical engineering.

 - PhD in physics modeling or battery chemistry preferred.

 - A world-class ownership mindset: you own outcomes, not just tasks.

 - Hands-on experience with battery modeling, ideally semi-empirical or physics-informed degradation models for lithium-ion cells.

 - Strong software and data skills: proficiency in Python and SQL (or equivalent).

 - Familiarity with cell testing and characterization (cycling, HPPC, EIS, or similar), and excitement about building a lab from the ground up.

 - Nice to have: experience with field or fleet data from deployed energy storage, EVs, or consumer electronics.




ABOUT THE TEAM

Base’s Modeling team owns how we understand the health and performance of our battery fleet. Every battery we deploy is a long-lived asset, and how it ages determines how we operate it, how it supports the grid, and how much value it creates for our members over its life. As the fleet grows across more homes, climates, and operating conditions, that question gets harder and more valuable to answer. This team gets to build Base’s degradation modeling capability from the ground up, from a new cell characterization lab to models running on fleet-scale telemetry, so we can predict how our batteries will age and make better decisions about every battery in the field.



Please note: Base is a startup, which means priorities shift and evolve quickly. Your role may expand or change based on the needs of the business at any given time, so the responsibilities listed may not be exhaustive.




OUR VALUES

 - First Principles Thinking: Question assumptions. Principles > rules.

 - Operate at Base Pace: Focus on what matters, act quickly, and learn by doing.

 - Give & Get Feedback: Be direct, be humble, and maintain a growth mindset.

 - Everyone’s an Owner: Follow through on commitments and own results.

 - Strong Opinions, Loosely Held: Drive clarity and make calls with imperfect information.

 - Committed to the Mission: Rebuilding the grid is a big challenge. We work hard because we care deeply about the impact we’re creating. We work in-person. It’s not a 9-to-5. We are all-in.

 - Fun & Optimism Coexist with Grit: Collaboration and celebration coincide with the intensity of building real things.
   
   


DO THE BEST WORK OF YOUR LIFE AT BASE.

3-5+ years of experience in a manufacturing operations role (e.g. Plant or Production Manager/Supervisor/Process Engineering Leader) in a manufacturing or production operations environment.

We’re building this company from the ground up, and every person we hire has an outsized impact on our culture, performance, and trajectory. While each team member brings unique strengths and perspectives, we look for people who align with our Operating Principles and embody them in action. If this sounds like you, Formic may be the right place for you!
Fearless Optimism: You make bold bets and default optimistic. You believe in the mission, aren’t paralyzed by risk, and fear inaction more than failure. You see ambiguity as opportunity and bring energy to building what doesn’t yet exist.

You will work with one to three small cross-functional teams (“pods”) where collaboration, trust, and ownership drive the team forward while engaging in the Agile @ Scale framework at Kraft Heinz.

Set technical direction for assigned innovation initiatives, translating ambiguous concepts and consumer or business needs into technical roadmaps, testable hypotheses, and clear success criteria.

title: Quality Assurance Associate
description:
Passionate about precision medicine and advancing the healthcare industry?
Recent advancements in underlying technology have finally made it possible for AI to impact clinical care in a meaningful way. Tempus' proprietary platform connects an entire ecosystem of real-world evidence to deliver real-time, actionable insights to physicians, providing critical information about the right treatments for the right patients, at the right time.
Job Description
Passionate about making a difference in the world of cancer genomics? With the advent of genomic sequencing, we can finally decode and process our genetic makeup. We now have more data than ever before but providers don't have the infrastructure or expertise to make sense of this data. We're on a mission to connect an entire ecosystem to redefine how genomic data is used in clinical settings.
We are looking for a Senior Quality Assurance Associate or Quality Assurance Associate who will be responsible for documenting and tracking compliance for a clinical molecular laboratory.  This individual will play an integral role in supporting quality assurance activities in accordance with FDA QMSR (Quality Management System Regulation), ISO 13485, and other applicable global regulations, including but not limited to records management, acceptance activities, production and process control. This individual also supports the QMS activities that comply with CLIA/CAP requirements for the clinical laboratories.
The shift for this position is Sunday to Thursday OR Tuesday to Saturday.

Compilation of the Device History Record.
Read and understand SOPs within the document control system.
File quality records in a systematic organized manner.
Maintain documentation in order to satisfy CLIA/CAP/NYS-DOH/FDA requirements.
Aid in tracking and maintenance of quality records, including batch records, checklists, and quality and equipment binders.
Report significant deviations and system deficiencies to management, under guidance and as appropriate.
Pull records and reports as requested during internal and external audits.
Help facilitate and implement corrective and preventative actions.

Assist in document control workflow, as needed.
Manage Supplier Documentation and Compliance, as needed: Proactively work with suppliers to ensure documentation on file is up to date
Send and Review Supplier Questionnaires
Maintain supplier certificates
Review and escalate customer and supplier notifications
Review documents received and escalate any concerns for further review

High school diploma, Bachelor's Degree in Life Science or Engineering preferred

Highly organized and systematic, with superb attention to detail
Ability to complete repetitive tasks with a high degree of precision and accuracy
Proven ability to learn new skills quickly and adapt to new processes smoothly
Good time management and communication skills
Self-driven and works well in a fast-moving, cross-functional team environment with minimal direction
Beginner ability to create processes, as well as suggest solutions to challenges

Previous experience in a clinical lab regulated by CAP/CLIA/NYS/FDA highly desirable

title: Director of IT & Infrastructure
description:
Via is on a mission to create public transportation systems that provide far greater access to jobs, healthcare, and education. Our platform serves as the technology backbone for modern transit networks, transforming antiquated and siloed public transportation systems into smart, data-driven, and efficient digital networks.
As Director of IT & Infrastructure , you’ll lead the team, systems, and infrastructure that keep our employees connected and our operations moving. Your scope will span global IT support, enterprise applications, identity and access, corporate networks, and the setup of facilities for new transit service launches.
This role combines excellent people leadership with hands-on technical expertise. Balancing an entrepreneurial spirit with a pragmatic approach to problem-solving, you will serve as a key stakeholder in building the reliable services our teams and partners depend on. From improving employee support through automation and AI to getting a new operational site ready for launch, you’ll turn complex requirements into well-run systems and repeatable processes.
What You’ll Do:
Lead our global IT team. Develop and support the team, establish clear ownership and service expectations, and translate business priorities into an actionable IT roadmap. Balance daily operations with infrastructure improvements and longer-term projects.
Own the employee IT experience. Oversee support across offices, remote teams, and operational sites. Lead the administration and continuous improvement of Freshservice , including ticketing, the service catalog, approvals, inventory, knowledge management, and automated workflows.
Manage identity and access. Oversee Okta , SSO, application provisioning, and employee onboarding, transfers, and offboarding. Maintain reliable access approval and provisioning workflows between Freshservice, Okta, and connected applications.
Run dependable infrastructure. Oversee corporate networks, Wi-Fi, internet connectivity, remote access, and IT-managed infrastructure. Use platforms such as Cisco Meraki to monitor sites, address outages, and improve reliability. Manage relevant DNS, domain, and certificate requirements, including work with Cloudflare, AWS, GCP .
Deliver Network TaaS launch readiness. Own facility setup and IT readiness for new launches, from sourcing telecommunications providers and infrastructure contractors to overseeing onsite installations, security cameras, and physical access control systems. Ensure access to company applications reflects each launch’s staffing and operational requirements.
Manage the endpoint and asset lifecycle. Establish hardware standards and oversee device deployment, management, support, inventory, purchasing, logistics, replacement, and secure disposal for a
Keep enterprise applications working together. Oversee platforms including Google Workspace, Slack, Jira, and Confluence, Freshservice, Iru and more , and partner with business owners on departmental systems. Lead implementations, migrations, and consolidation projects with clear support and administrative ownership.
Build better workflows through automation and AI. Expand integrations across Freshservice, Okta, Slack, Confluence, and other services. Develop and maintain bots and AI agents that answer employee questions, use company knowledge, and handle service requests, with appropriate monitoring and controls.
Support practical AI adoption. Manage the rollout and administration of tools such as Claude and Cursor , including employee access, licensing, usage allocations, spending visibility, and support.
Manage technology spending and suppliers. Own IT budget planning and tracking, vendor relationships, commercial negotiations, renewals, and license optimization. Lead technical assessments within ZIP procurement workflows alongside Procurement, Finance, Legal, and Information Security.
Strengthen security and operational continuity. Partner with Information Security to implement controls across IT-managed systems, support audits and access reviews, and address control gaps. Maintain recovery procedures, system documentation, and backup ownership for critical services.
Who You Are:
An experienced IT leader with 10+ years in corporate IT or infrastructure , including 4+ years managing teams , ideally in a global technology company.
A hands-on technical leader who can move comfortably between coaching a team, planning a deployment, troubleshooting an integration, and managing a vendor escalation.
Experienced in identity and access management, SaaS administration, endpoint management, networking, and IT service delivery. Familiarity with Okta, Google Workspace, Cisco Meraki, and Freshservice , or comparable platforms, will help you succeed.
Comfortable delivering technology infrastructure for new offices or operational sites, including coordinating connectivity providers, contractors, and installation schedules.
Skilled at improving processes through APIs, integrations, and automation, with practical experience applying AI to internal support or employee workflows.
Commercially minded, with experience managing budgets, negotiating with suppliers, and improving software and hardware spending.
A clear communicator who builds strong working relationships across Operations, Engineering, Information Security, People, Finance, and other business teams.
Organized, resourceful, and comfortable managing competing priorities in a fast-moving environment. You follow problems through to resolution and build processes that help prevent them from recurring.
Via is an equal opportunity employer.

title: Field Operations Manager
description:
Via is using technology to transform transportation around the world. From changing a single person’s daily commute to reducing humanity’s collective environmental footprint — we’ve got huge goals.
As a Field Operations Manager on Via’s Transit-as-a-Service (TaaS) Operations team, you will oversee day-to-day operations using our technology platform, ensuring smooth and reliable service as Via expands across the UK . Your focus will be specifically on our Westlink service , where you will drive continuous improvement and operational excellence, helping to deliver a positive experience for our passengers and supporting the growth of the service.
This is an in-person position with the expectation that you will be onsite 4-5 days per week.
About the Role:
Run daily onsite operations, ensuring safe, reliable, and accessible transportation for our riders.
Partner with a broad, cross-functional team to develop and scale the processes, systems, and tools that drive continuous optimization and support rapid growth.
Make real-time decisions on fleet, driver supply, compliance, rider needs, and unexpected issues - using data to quickly diagnose problems and keep service running smoothly.
Guide and support drivers, building strong relationships and coaching toward stronger performance in the field.
Turn rider and community feedback into concrete changes by spotting patterns and addressing root causes.
Act as the bridge between Via’s partners, drivers, and Via central teams, keeping everyone informed with clear, timely updates and resolving questions quickly.
About You:
Operationally experienced in people management, logistics, customer service, or other process-oriented work.
Relationship-oriented and a confident communicator who builds trust with drivers, riders, teammates, and city partners, adapting their message and tone to each stakeholder, whether that’s partners, customers, or driver colleagues from diverse backgrounds.
Hands-on and proactive, comfortable taking responsibility for employees, being in the field, and solving problems where they happen, even under pressure.
Analytically savvy and structured, using data and digital tools to prioritize effectively and improve our services.
Tactical and strategic, able to tackle issues in real time while thinking ahead and building solutions that prevent them from recurring.
Fluent in English.
Valid driver’s license in the UK, class B.
Nice to have, but not required: Completed Certificate of Professional Competence (CPC) training and Qualified Transport Manager status would be a plus, as would experience in fixed-line bus operations.
Compensation and Benefits:
Becoming part of a company that was awarded for its commitment to social good.
Salary Range: £40,000–£45,000. Final salary will be determined by the candidate’s experience, knowledge, and skills.
Comprehensive health scheme offered through AXA.
Partnership with YellowNest, a salary exchange benefit that helps reduce childcare fees for working parents.
Cycle to Work Scheme - multiple options via Green Commute Initiative (GCI).
There has never been a more exciting time to be on the cutting edge of public mobility. Ready to join the ride?
Via is an equal opportunity employer.
